key_insight: A low-pressure xenon plasma cell can convert deep-UV laser light to electricity with very high simulated efficiency by using photoionization plus magnetically guided charge separation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new receiver architecture for space laser power beaming that could avoid many heat-loss mechanisms that limit semiconductor photovoltaic systems.
method: Particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulation of a low-pressure xenon chamber
58.4 nm pulsed laser driving xenon photoionization
Magnetic bias and chamber parameter scans to optimize charge collection
evidence_signal: The simulations report 82.25% steady-state laser-to-electrical conversion efficiency at 2000 W/m2 average incident power, with energy accounting closing to 1%.
watch_item: The result is a proof-of-concept from simulation, so practical deployment will depend on achieving stable photon absorption, electron confinement, and low-loss operation in a real space hardware system.
paper_title: Laser power transmission in space: Plasma-based power cell
